findings.reason: The protected recursive sources are algorithmically correct but rely on Python's default recursion limit even though the verified contract permits a 100,000-node skewed tree. A direct legal-shape probe with 1,500 nodes raises RecursionError in the protected app-local source.

The inert candidate simulates the same postorder return recurrence with explicit `(node, state, left)` frames and one child-result register. It returns the correct ancestor on the 1,500-node probe, preserves O(n) time and O(h) space, and avoids changing either protected source or submission evidence.

Legal 31/127/511-node complete-tree tiers place the targets at opposite extreme leaves, forcing both sides to contribute. The candidate passes at +0.13 relative exponent and 3.87x largest ratio; a correct subtree-membership search over every possible ancestor passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.25.

The Approach now targets the candidate exactly: it defines each subtree report, explains all three frame states and the result register, proves the two-report meeting rule, and accounts for O(h) explicit frames without call-stack dependence.
